findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category is not set in the database
findings.body: The migration unconditionally does execute(...)[0]['id'] for the embed_category lookup. On a fresh install, or any site that never changed embed_category (site_settings only stores non-default values), that query returns zero rows, so [0] is nil and nil['id'] raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration and leaving the upgrade half-applied. The same pattern on line 15 for uncategorized_category_id has the same problem. The lookup needs to handle an empty result before indexing into it.

findings.title: Migration interpolates stored host values directly into SQL and stores them unsanitized
findings.body: Each line from the old embeddable_hosts setting is interpolated unescaped into an INSERT statement ('#{h}'). A host value containing a single quote breaks the migration, and a crafted value can inject arbitrary SQL executed with the migration's privileges. Additionally the raw value is stored verbatim, so legacy entries like 'http://discourse.org' or 'https://example.com/1234' (both valid in the old setting) are stored with scheme/path intact; EmbeddableHost.record_for_host compares them against URI(host).host, which never equals such a string, so those hosts silently stop being allowed after migration. The values should be inserted with quoting/bound parameters and normalized the same way the model normalizes them (strip scheme and path).

findings.title: before_validation crashes when host is nil
findings.body: The before_validation block calls self.host.sub! without checking for nil, and there is no presence validation evaluated before this callback. Creating a host with a missing host parameter (Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host assigns params[:embeddable_host][:host], which is nil when the key is absent) raises NoMethodError instead of failing validation and returning a JSON error, producing a 500.

findings.title: Duplicate and case-variant hosts are allowed, making category selection nondeterministic
findings.body: There is no uniqueness validation on host. An admin can create two embeddable_hosts rows for the same hostname (including case variants, since stored case is preserved and matching lowercases only the column side) pointing at different categories. EmbeddableHost.record_for_host then returns .first with no ORDER BY, so which category embedded topics land in, and effectively which row governs the host, is arbitrary database order. A case-insensitive uniqueness validation (and matching index) is needed.

findings.title: Host validation permits ports and rejects long TLDs, inconsistent with host matching
findings.body: The format regex explicitly allows a port (':[0-9]{1,5}') and paths, but record_for_host matches against URI(referer).host, which excludes the port, so a validated host like 'example.com:3000' can never match and embedding from it is always rejected. Conversely the regex limits the TLD to 2-5 letters, so legitimate hosts on newer/longer TLDs (e.g. .technology, .international) cannot be added at all. The accepted format and the matching logic need to agree.

findings.title: Update and destroy crash with a 500 for a nonexistent host id
findings.body: Both update and destroy use EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and immediately call save_host(host) or host.destroy without a nil check. A stale admin UI (e.g. a host deleted in another tab) or a hand-crafted request with an unknown id therefore raises NoMethodError on nil instead of returning a 404. save_host also dereferences params[:embeddable_host] without checking its presence, with the same 500-on-malformed-request problem.

findings.title: Edit action crashes when a host has no resolvable category
findings.body: The edit action does this.get('host.category.id') unconditionally. host.category is only populated by the store's embedded hydration via Discourse.Category.findById(category_id); if the referenced category was deleted or is not among the site's loaded categories, category is undefined and clicking edit throws a TypeError, making the row impossible to edit or fix from the UI. The same assumption appears on save (line 38), where a blank categoryId sets host.category to undefined even though the server silently substitutes the uncategorized category, so the row displays no category until reload.

findings.title: Fabricator file contents are swapped between category and embeddable_host files
findings.body: category_fabricator.rb now defines only Fabricator(:embeddable_host), while the newly added embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains all the category fabricators (:category, :diff_category, :happy_category, :private_category). Fabrication loads every file so tests still pass, but the swapped contents are misleading for future maintainers editing or adding fabricators, and any tooling that loads fabricator files selectively by name will register the wrong definitions. The contents should be moved back into their eponymous files.
